summary: The agency accepted several manufacturer comments—incorporating California emission standard effects, revising noble metal discussion, and providing two NPA classes and a range of fuel economies—but rejected the weight-reduction impossibility argument for GM and dropped the sulfate emissions discussion.
text:
As a result of the analysis of all comments the agency is making several changes to the draft EIS. Gasoline savings are described in this final EIS relative to a range of fuel economies. The range was established by applying the maximum and minimum possible fuel economy penalties of the MY 1979 emission standard to the originally proposed AFES. Also, gasoline savings are shown for two classes of NPA's. The two classes are 1) recreational type NPA's with off-road capability and 2) all other NPA's.

The effects of the MY 1979 emission standard for California, according to the information applied by the domestic manufacturers, are incorporated. The manufacturers' comments on the impossibility of weight reduction are not incorporated because the application of weight reduction is only to GM and they did not say it was impossible. The discussion of sulfate emissions has been dropped and the discussion of noble metal use has been revised to indicate a smaller increase in the use of platinum and palladium. Minor changes have been made to the sections on noise emissions and increased use of plastics.
